title: Liverpool’s Giorgi Mamardashvili to miss at least two weeks but knee injury not serious
content:
Giorgi Mamardashvili’s injury is not as bad as first feared but the Liverpool goalkeeper is still expected to spend at least a fortnight on the sidelines.

Mamardashvili is out of hospital and recovering after suffering a deep wound to his knee in a collision with Everton striker Beto during Sunday’s Merseyside derby at Hill Dickinson Stadium, which Arne Slot’s side won 2-1.

An exact timeframe has not yet been put on the 25-year-old’s return, but it is expected to be between two and four weeks, depending on the speed of his recovery.

The Georgia international sustained the injury in a clash ahead of Beto’s 54th-minute equaliser.

Posting on Instagram earlier on Monday, Mamardashvili wrote: “Thank God everything is fine. Thank you all so much for your support and for being by my side. I’ll be back soon.”

With No 1 Alisson still sidelined by a hamstring problem, Slot had to hand a Premier League debut to third-choice keeper Freddie Woodman at the weekend. The former Preston North End goalkeeper, who kept a clean sheet in his minutes against Everton, is now expected to start against former club Crystal Palace this weekend.

Mamardashvili would also be likely to miss the visit to Manchester United on May 3, and could also be unavailable for the clash against Chelsea six days later, on May 9.

Alisson, meanwhile, is targeting a return to action for the match against United at Old Trafford.

After Sunday’s game, head coach Slot said of Mamardashvili: “Is there anything that surprises you when it comes to injuries with us this season?”

“Maybe I already envisaged it because I had two goalkeepers on the bench today, which I normally don’t have but, of course, it has everything to do with the availability of all the other positions.

“Giorgi had to go to hospital with a big wound, so let’s see how he will be. Freddie deserves a lot of credit — coming in just after conceding at 1-1 and their fans were ready for it but he did his job really well.”

The positive news for Liverpool and Mamardashvili is that this injury is not as serious as it looked when he left the pitch on a stretcher.

Slot spoke after the game to ease some of those fears but it was still a nervous wait for the Georgian goalkeeper as he spent the night in hospital awaiting results.

Mamardashvili has been filling in for Alisson and performed well in the Merseyside derby so there were understandable fears when he was replaced by Woodman, a goalkeeper who hasn’t played a single minute in the Premier League this season.

To his credit, Woodman was calm and composed as he was thrown into the heat of such an intense fixture, and that performance provided a soothing reassurance ahead of the weekend, when he’s going to be needed again. It also shows the importance of having three senior goalkeepers in the squad.

Liverpool have been plagued by injuries this season and still have five important games remaining. Having Mamardashvili back available for some of those will help, but the most important part is that he won’t be missing for a long period like some of his team-mates.
